web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What growth, margin durability, and governance risk discount do the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close (₹1,842.40) and 2026-11-25 live TradingView price (₹1,859.90) embed, and how does Manorama stack up against listed Indian specialty peers?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a high-ROCE compounder trades above forty times earnings during an executive transition and a Sahel capex ramp, you are no longer buying yesterday's factory—you are underwriting tomorrow's governance and reinvestment discipline.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, Manorama closed at ₹1,842.40, down 14.74% from its ₹2,161.00 52-week high [39]. On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView tape, shares traded at ₹1,859.90 [39]. That implies a ₹11,623.67 crore market cap on TradingView (₹11,740 crore on Screener) [1, 39]. Shares trade at 41.15x TradingView TTM P/E (41.3x Screener) and 8.84x book value (₹210 per share) [1, 39]. Note that TTM Other Income jumped 3x to ₹30 crore (from ₹10 crore in FY26) on idle QIP treasury interest, adding ~₹15 crore after tax (~5.2% of ₹284 crore TTM PAT) and flattering headline TTM P/E [1, 22].

Two forces explain the pullback from November 13's 48.03x multiple at ₹1,984.10 [27, 39]. On growth, Q2 FY27 sales rose 41.9% YoY to ₹458.86 crore (~85% volume-led, ~85% plant utilization) [33, 35]. PAT jumped 51.8% to ₹80.81 crore, and EBITDA margin held 25.8% despite ~140 bps of freight drag [33, 35]. On risk, Pass 1 flagged the Nov 12 handover to MD Deep Saraf and Chairman Mudit Kumar Singh as founders moved to non-board President roles [32]. It also found a ₹20.64 crore Customs Section 108 deposit, ₹200 crore FY27 Manorama Africa RPTs, and up to ₹350 crore in Burkina Faso commitments amid shea export bans [36, 37]. Below, we bridge FY28E earnings strictly to physical capacity and test what ₹1,859.90 prices in.

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF & Capacity-Bridged Valuation: What ₹1,859.90 Already Prices In

web_blocks.html: We start from FY26 sales of ₹1,367 crore (TTM ₹1,617 crore) and ~6.31 crore post-QIP shares [1, 30]. We run a 10-year Reverse DCF at a 12.0% WACC (up 50 bps for Sahel and handover risk) and 5.0% terminal growth [32, 37]. CRISIL confirmed zero deviations in the ₹485.40 crore net (₹500 crore gross) QIP cash [35]. Because that cash offsets mid-cycle debt, ₹11,623.67 crore market cap equals enterprise value [39]. Earning 12.0% a year at a flat multiple requires ~19.5% sales growth for ten years (~₹8,100 crore by FY36) at 22.0% average OPM.

Physical Capacity Bridge (FY28E): Birkoni's existing 47,500 MTPA fractionation plant ran at ~85% utilization in Q2 FY27 (₹458.86 crore quarterly sales, or ~₹1,835 crore annualized) [5, 33]. Pushing existing lines to 90%–95% utilization yields ~₹1,945–₹2,050 crore in annual sales. Because Solvent Fractionation-3 (SF-3) is not targeted until ~Q3 FY28, FY28E captures only a partial Q3–Q4 commissioning ramp [22, 35]. Our Base Case therefore bridges FY28E revenue to ~₹2,050 crore (22.5% CAGR), normalizes OPM to 22.5%–23.0% (22.8% midpoint, ₹467 crore OP), and strips temporary QIP treasury income to reach ~₹305 crore FY28E PAT (~₹48.4 EPS). Applying a peer-aligned 35.0x exit P/E (matching Fine Organic's 35.5x) yields ₹1,692 core value plus ~₹108/share net QIP/SF-3 CWIP credit—a ₹1,700–₹1,850 fair-value band anchored at our ₹1,800 Base Target.

web_blocks.caption: Capacity-Bridged FY28E Valuation & Red Team Stress Matrix (2026-11-25 Live TV ₹1,859.90 | 2026-11-23 Ledger ₹1,842.40 | ~6.31 Cr Shares)
web_blocks.takeaway: Bridging FY28E strictly to 47,500 MTPA capacity (~₹2,050 Cr sales, 22.8% OPM, ~₹305 Cr PAT) at Fine Organic's peer-aligned 35.0x P/E (₹1,692 core + ~₹108/sh QIP/SF-3 credit) puts Base Target and Probability-Weighted EV at ₹1,800 (-3.2% vs live TV). Bear Case sits at ₹1,150 (-38.2%) and Red Team 30x/20% OPM stress at ₹1,267 (-31.9%).

web_blocks.title: Head-to-Head Peer Valuation & Return Quality (2026-11-25 Live Snapshot)

web_blocks.html: Comparing Manorama against listed Indian specialty-ingredient peers tests whether its 41.15x trailing multiple is backed by durable return quality or stretched by peak margins. Fine Organic Industries is the closest B2B food-additive and oleochemical benchmark, while Clean Science & Technology and Galaxy Surfactants anchor specialty-chemical margin durability and multiple compression risk. Together, these three peers show what the Indian market pays once rapid capex phases normalize.

web_blocks.caption: Listed Indian Specialty Ingredients & Oleochemicals Peer Snapshot (2026-11-25 Live TradingView / Screener)
web_blocks.takeaway: At 41.15x TV P/E (41.3x Screener), Manorama trades ~16% above Fine Organic (35.53x, 21.5% ROCE), while Clean Science (31.51x) and Galaxy Surfactants (17.41x) sit in Stage 4.

web_blocks.html: The live 2026-11-25 peer table confirms why a 35.0x exit multiple is far more disciplined than 40.0x [39]. Fine Organic (FINEORG) trades at ₹5,582.50 (₹17,178 crore cap), or 35.53x TV P/E (35.5x Screener) with 20.44% OPM, 21.5% ROCE, and 12.93% TTM sales growth [39]. Clean Science (CLEAN) trades at ₹691.40 (31.51x TV P/E, 26.42% OPM, 20.7% ROCE, 4.51% growth) in Stage 4 [39]. Galaxy Surfactants (GALAXYSURF) trades at ₹1,994.50 (17.41x TV P/E, 8.74% OPM, 14.79% ROE), also in Stage 4 [39].

Manorama's higher ROCE (34.9% vs Fine Organic's 21.5%) and 40%+ volume growth explain its current ~16% P/E premium [1, 33, 39]. Yet peer history shows peak multiples rarely hold when margins normalize or capex nears full utilization. Stripping out ₹30 crore of temporary TTM Other Income makes core trailing P/E even richer (~43x). Local rivals 3F Industries and AAK India (ILLEXAO EN 10) also test spreads as NY cocoa cools near $5,300/tonne (London ~£3,975–£4,147/tonne on Nov 23–25) [34, 38].

web_blocks.mechanism: Supply tightness lifted specialty food-additive margins from ~19% to >26% in FY23, and the market paid 45x–50x P/E. When supply eased, margins fell back toward 20–22% and the P/E compressed to ~33x–35x over two years.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: OPM peaked near 26.5% in FY23 before easing to ~20.4% TTM; P/E fell from ~48x to 35.5x.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even strong B2B moats de-rate when peak margins normalize. Anchoring Base Case to 22.5%–23.0% OPM and a peer-aligned 35.0x exit P/E prevents paying peak multiples for mid-cycle earnings.

web_blocks.title: Independent Valuation Judgment (Nov 25 Refresh)
paragraphs: At ₹1,859.90 (2026-11-25 live TV; ₹1,842.40 on 2026-11-23 ledger), Manorama trades at 41.15x TV P/E—flattered slightly by ₹30 Cr of TTM Other Income from idle QIP cash. Bridging FY28E strictly to Birkoni's 47,500 MTPA ceiling plus partial Q3–Q4 SF-3 ramp (~₹2,050 Cr sales, 22.8% OPM, ~₹305 Cr PAT / ₹48.4 EPS) at Fine Organic's 35.0x exit P/E (₹1,692 core + ~₹108/sh QIP/SF-3 credit) puts Base Target and Probability-Weighted EV at ₹1,800 (-3.2% vs live TV). With zero margin of safety above CMP and -31.9% to -38.2% Bear/Red-Team downside (₹1,267 / ₹1,150), new capital is REJECTED on valuation.

web_blocks.html: Valuation trigger: revisit our ₹1,800 Base Target upward only if SF-3 commissions ahead of Q3 FY28 with confirmed >24% core OPM, or downgrade further if OPM falls below 20.0% for two quarters or Customs/RPT liabilities escalate.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I can finally open the price tape—and this refresh gives us a textbook lesson in why separating business quality from market price is so valuable. Throughout Chapters 1 through 6, we kept the stock quote locked outside the room while we audited both the growth engine and the newly uncovered risks. Manorama Industries still clears our COMPOUNDER_PASS hurdle on its 47,500 MTPA Birkoni fractionation scale (~85% utilized in Q2 FY27), 34.9% ROCE, 92% FY26 CFO-to-EBITDA conversion, and ₹500 crore QIP balance-sheet cushion with zero deviations per CRISIL. Yet our Pass 1 blind-spot audit also forced three material governance and geopolitical watchpoints onto the table: the November 12, 2026 transition from founders Ashish Ramesh Saraf (formerly Chairman & MD) and Vinita Ashish Saraf (formerly Vice Chairperson & WTD) to Managing Director Deep Saraf and Chairman Mudit Kumar Singh; the ₹20.64 crore Customs Act Section 108 deposit on UAE Palm Mid Fraction imports alongside ₹200 crore FY27 related-party purchases from promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited; and West African raw shea export bans and Burkina Faso's CFA 200/kg levy pushing up to ₹350 crore of subsidiary capital commitments into the Sahel.

With that full ledger in hand, what is the market asking us to pay? On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, Manorama settled at ₹1,842.40—down 14.74% from its 52-week high of ₹2,161.00. On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, shares ticked up to ₹1,859.90, valuing the company at ₹11,623.67 crore (₹11,740 crore on Screener). That puts the stock at 41.15 times TradingView trailing earnings (41.3 times Screener consolidated P/E) and 8.84 times book value (₹210 per share). And notice a subtle forensic wrinkle from Chapter 6: while FY26 Other Income fell to ₹10 crore, TTM Other Income through September 2026 jumped threefold to ₹30 crore on temporary treasury interest from idle QIP cash, adding roughly ₹15 crore after tax (~5.2% of ₹284 crore TTM PAT) and making core operating P/E closer to 43x.

Let's run our Reverse DCF on ₹1,859.90 without rose-tinted glasses. Starting from FY26 audited revenue of ₹1,367 crore (TTM ₹1,617 crore through September 2026) and roughly 6.31 crore post-QIP diluted shares, we raise our discount rate by 50 basis points to a 12.0% WACC (from 11.5% previously) and keep terminal growth at 5.0%. Why raise WACC? Because committing up to ₹350 crore into Burkina Faso's Taang Kaam Industries SA amid Sahel export levies—while transitioning Board executive control—deserves a higher equity risk premium. Because the ₹485.40 crore net QIP proceeds roughly offset mid-cycle seasonal working-capital debt, ₹11,623.67 crore of market cap approximates enterprise value. To earn a 12.0% annual return from ₹1,859.90 with zero multiple expansion, Manorama must compound sales at roughly 19.5% a year for a decade (reaching ~₹8,100 crore by FY36), sustain average normalized EBITDA margins near 22.0%, and cap incremental working-capital absorption below 28% of new revenue.

Before assuming 28% near-term revenue growth, however, we have to respect physical steel and concrete at Birkoni. Existing 47,500 MTPA fractionation is already running near 85% utilization in Q2 FY27 (₹458.86 crore sales, or ~₹1,835 crore annualized). Pushing those existing lines to 90%–95% utilization caps annual revenue near ₹1,945–₹2,050 crore, and Solvent Fractionation-3 is not scheduled to commission until roughly Q3 FY28. That means FY28E gets at most one to two quarters of partial SF-3 contribution—and any two-quarter slip like FY24 eliminates FY28E expansion volume altogether. Bridging revenue honestly to physical capacity puts Base FY28E sales at ~₹2,050 crore (22.5% CAGR from FY26), not ₹2,240 crore.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Live Peer Table: Why 35.0x Beats 40.0x
paragraphs: When we benchmark Manorama against three live listed Indian specialty peers as of November 25, 2026, the multiple ceiling becomes unmistakable. Fine Organic Industries (FINEORG)—still the closest B2B food-ingredient cousin—rallied to ₹5,582.50 (₹17,178 crore market cap), trading at 35.53x TradingView TTM P/E (35.5x Screener) on 20.44% operating margins, 21.5% Screener ROCE, and 12.93% TTM revenue growth. Clean Science & Technology (CLEAN) sits in a Stage 4 downtrend at ₹691.40 (31.51x P/E, 26.42% OPM, 20.7% ROCE, 4.51% TTM revenue growth). Galaxy Surfactants (GALAXYSURF) also trades in Stage 4 at ₹1,994.50 (17.41x P/E, 8.74% OPM, 14.79% ROE).

At 41.15x TradingView P/E, Manorama commands a ~16% multiple premium over Fine Organic while delivering a 13.4-percentage-point ROCE advantage (34.9% vs 21.5%) and more than triple Fine Organic's top-line growth rate. Still, remember Fine Organic's 2021–2024 valuation lesson: when specialty food-additive margins spiked above 26% in FY23, the market bid Fine Organic near 48x earnings, only to spend two years compressing the multiple back to 35.5x as margins settled near 20.4%. Against unlisted domestic rivals 3F Industries Ltd. and AAK India (which launched ILLEXAO EN 10 in June 2025) and easing cocoa futures (~$5,300/tonne NY), paying 40x FY28E earnings leaves zero margin of safety. Matching Fine Organic's 35.0x peer exit multiple is the honest benchmark.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Good underwriting checks physical factory tonnage and peer multiple history before falling in love with a spreadsheet CAGR. Bridging FY28E strictly to Birkoni's 47,500 MTPA ceiling and Fine Organic's 35.0x exit P/E pulls Base fair value straight down to ₹1,800—below today's ₹1,859.90 quote.

book_subsections.title: Capacity-Bridged Three-Scenario Valuation & Red Team Stress Test
paragraphs: We recalibrate all three FY28E scenarios around Birkoni's physical tonnage ceiling, normalized margins, and peer-aligned exit multiples. In our Base Case (50% probability), existing 47,500 MTPA lines run at 90%–95% utilization alongside a partial Q3–Q4 FY28 Solvent Fractionation-3 ramp to generate ~₹2,050 crore of FY28E revenue (22.5% CAGR from FY26). Normalizing operating margin to 22.5%–23.0% (22.8% midpoint, ₹467 crore operating profit) and stripping temporary ₹30 crore TTM QIP treasury interest yields ~₹305 crore of FY28E PAT (~₹48.4 EPS on 6.31 crore shares). Applying Fine Organic's peer-aligned 35.0x exit P/E values core FY28E earnings at ₹1,692 per share; adding ~₹108 per share of net QIP/SF-3 CWIP value for the FY29 ramp frames a ₹1,700–₹1,850 fair-value band anchored at our ₹1,800 Base Target (-3.2% vs live TV ₹1,859.90; -2.3% vs ledger ₹1,842.40).

In our Bull Case (25% probability), Deep Saraf delivers Solvent Fractionation-3 ahead of schedule, Burkina Faso local processing turns the CFA 200/kg levy into a supply moat, and revenue reaches ₹2,350 crore (31.1% CAGR) at 24.5% OPM (₹576 crore OP), generating ₹396 crore of PAT (₹62.8 EPS) valued at 39.0x for a ₹2,450 target (+31.7% vs live TV). In our Bear Case (25% probability), SF-3 slips, cocoa spread normalization and rivals AAK India and 3F Industries cap revenue at ₹1,875 crore (17.1% CAGR) and compress OPM to 20.0% (₹375 crore OP), yielding ₹242 crore of PAT (₹38.4 EPS) at 30.0x—taking shares down to ₹1,150 (-38.2% vs live TV). We also explicitly publish our Red Team Bear Stress (₹2,000 crore sales, 20.0% OPM, ₹266.5 crore PAT at 30.0x), which lands at ₹1,267 (-31.9% vs live TV). Weighting Bull (25%), Base (50%), and Bear (25%) yields a probability-weighted expected value of exactly ₹1,800 (-3.2% vs live TV)—well below our 12.0% WACC hurdle and an unmistakable valuation rejection for fresh capital.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing Post-QIP Dilution, Customs Exposure, and Sahel Capital
paragraphs: Let's stress-test the exact rupees behind our Pass 1 forensic findings so we neither dismiss nor exaggerate them. The ₹20.64 crore Customs Act Section 108 deposit equals just 0.18% of Manorama's ₹11,624 crore market cap and ~7.3% of TTM net profit—hardly balance-sheet fatal on its own, even if supplier recovery fails. What matters is the signaling and governance effect: combined with the delayed SPA/RBI buyout of promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited (₹200 crore FY27 RPT limit) and the jump in pledged margin-money deposits from ₹49.26 lakh to ₹982.46 lakh, institutional investors will demand spotless disclosure from new MD Deep Saraf and auditor Singhi & Co. before awarding a 40x+ multiple again.

Similarly, up to ₹350 crore approved for Burkina Faso subsidiary Taang Kaam Industries SA represents a meaningful slice of net worth, funded indirectly by the ₹500 crore QIP equity buffer. Because the QIP was raised near cycle highs with modest ~5% dilution, it remains accretive if incremental Sahel and Birkoni capex earns above 22%–25% ROCE. If political disruption or export levies strand that capital, however, ROCE will mean-revert toward 20% and the stock will trade at 30x–35x specialty-processor multiples—right inside our ₹1,150–₹1,267 bear stress band.
